correctness.rationale: Valuation at prime 523 forces the second-largest factorial index into {523,524,525,526}, an exhaustive four-case reduction. Prime-signature equality is equivalent to the integer product being a square. Every increasing six-tuple is represented exactly once by its first two pairs and its final pair, and the exact pair lookup gives counts 5,0,1,126. The complete 132-row witness CSV is cross-checked by two independently computed prime-signature methods (integer factorization and Legendre formula) and opposite pair-lookup orders; both generate exactly the same complete sextuple set. No extrapolation beyond the finite domain.

value.rationale: At the historically established first n requiring six distinct factorials, the count of all shortest representations is a canonical extremal multiplicity, not a gratuitous parameter slice. The census determines the full witness space (132 tuples) and reveals its penultimate-index concentration (126 of 132 at 526), providing an exact benchmark for constructive searches and calibrating the extreme first six-factor example. This self-contained exact finite fact does not imply a general distribution theorem, nor is one asserted.
